newsitem.title: GERMANY: German wheat price rise deters buyers abroad.
newsitem.headline: German wheat price rise deters buyers abroad.

text.p: German new crop wheat prices have gained up to 7.50 marks on the week but there is no buying from southern or eastern Europe, brokers said.

They were concerned hasty pre-harvest buying from large trade houses had added to the nominal price so that consumers retreated and middlemen in the long marketing chain now had little room for manoeuvre.

"Exporters are jumping the gun," one complained. "They have accumulated volumes because of concern over volume and quality losses in Italy, Spain, Britain and northern France and they hope for sales to the flooded areas in eastern Europe."
"But there will be large harvests after all in Europe and the high price means country merchants and co-ops cannot count on a proper margin."
Farmers now expected high farmgate prices while farmgate buyers bore the price risks from possible harvest delays, drying, cleaning and storage costs, he explained.
There was talk more than 400,000 tonnes had been sold ahead of the harvest in the export-intensive northern coastal regions, with wheat harvesting a number of weeks away.
The Hamburg grain exchange raised its spot bread wheat price (220 Hagberg, 12.5 percent protein) by 2.50 marks a tonne to 267.50 but left the spot feed wheat price at 262.50 this week.
German fob levels for new crop wheat were starting at 272.50 for 12 percent Aug/Sept wheat in the 3,000 lot size.
A wide range of qualities, shipment sizes and dates up to December were available, with top prices for 10,000 tonnes Sept/Dec 14 percent wheat fob Rostock at 310 marks.
Barley prices were steady as good domestic yields and qualities exerted price pressure but this was overruled by the positive effect of third country export hopes. Half the harvest is now complete.
The July/Aug barley price is at around 245 marks fob and Sept/Dec cost 245-255.
New crop rye was also steady at 242.50-247.50 marks fob first half Sept. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
